chapter: Europe and South America with Sam Wooding
title: Berlin reception and the route through Europe
summary: The show was well received in Berlin despite objections, then toured Scandinavia, Central Europe, Spain and Russia before the group left the show in Paris.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Your first stops were in Germany?

Received wonderfully well. The people thought it was great. Some of the Germans still had their effects of World War I in their minds and they objected to us being there because they said they had so much trouble with the Senegalese during the war and they didn't want to see any more black people. They were very -- but the people by and large received us beautifully.
What type of places were they -- theaters?

Oh, yes, theaters, theaters. The Admiral's Palace was our first stop. Then we went to Hamburg to a big theater there, and from there we went to, I remember, Stockholm, Sweden, and we played the circus and there's where I met the Crown Prince. I had a letter from the crown prince of Sweden who's now the present King, and he was the head of the Red Cross then. We played concerts and special command performances for them there. Then we went to Denmark and Denmark was a fabulous town. It was more active than Paris in

those days. Then back to Germany and so into Budapest and Hungaria, Austria, Switzerland -- we went all over Switzerland. Italy, France, Spain -- we did all the big towns in Spain. And then we went to Russia.
You were booked by a promoter from Germany --

No, he was a Russian, his name was Nianof, he was a Russian. And we stayed with the show until after Russia and then we left the show in Paris, and then we were on our own and we started free lancing in Paris.
